lvuyk4:149: In the requirement self-iteration case, QA's right to refuse is a key emergence node. In practice, one should consciously design which roles can say "no" to other roles' outputs under what conditions: what are the admission criteria? After a refusal, how is the correction loop triggered? This mechanism is not defined once and done, but iterates continuously over multiple rounds of collaboration. It is recommended that each role have at least two explicit "refusal trigger conditions," and for each condition define a subsequent correction path.
m5bumi:210: Most AI Agent implementations stay at the "tool enhancement" level: they connect Agents to existing processes, making Agents more efficient, but without changing how the organization operates. Agent Room differs in that it places multiple roles into the same context field — product, QA, architecture, full-stack — allowing them to correct each other and make joint judgments within the same information. This requires organizations to not only support multi-Agent collaboration technically, but also to make systematic designs in role definitions, information sharing protocols, and decision transmission mechanisms. Tools can be replicated at zero cost, but context integration between roles requires continuous organizational investment.
nt9da:197: The core assumption of Agent Room is that "if multiple roles are placed in the same context field, they will judge for themselves whether they should intervene." But context sharing itself does not automatically produce collaboration—it requires mechanism design: when roles intervene (admission threshold), when to stay silent (avoid interference), and when to advance (loop completion). In Example 2, the technical support Agent did not stop at the surface conclusion "logs are normal," but continued to dig deeper, embodying the combination of shared context and proactive judgment. Without such a proactive intervention mechanism, the context is merely read-only material and will not produce collaborative behavior.
o583bn:210: In a traditional single-agent process, QA is a post-hoc verifier—development finishes, QA tests; multiple agents execute in sequence but lack lateral correction. In Agent Room, QA intervenes early, actively sets release preconditions, and rejects acceptance when admission criteria are not met. This is the first observable sign of emergent multi-agent collaboration: one role begins to exercise veto power over another role's output. This is not a process node predefined in advance, but QA, in the shared context, judges that "the current completed facts are insufficient to enter testing," and then @-mentions the developer to supplement evidence. This lateral constraint mechanism is core evidence of emergence.

r6ekta:229: The essence of the three-layer evolution is the leap from automation tools to collaborative judgment entities. In the first stage, Aone Agent turned the R&D process into a page-based interface; AI was an enhanced executor—the process was defined by humans, and AI only ran faster. In the second stage, OpenClaw achieved full-chain automation, where agents could read requirements, identify repositories, and infer tech stacks. But neither stage broke through the "tool" category. The essential leap of the third stage is that the system begins to grow a "brain" and can make decision judgments rather than merely executing preset paths. The key to this leap is not how many tools or CLIs are integrated, but whether multiple roles can form a true judgment loop within the same context.
